text:
inc-bot: paging: high 5xx rate detected from private-vpc-gateway-prod -> 504/timeouts from inference-gw cluster (elevated since 3345678840). paging: @oncall

Asha (oncall): I’m on it, grabbing logs and routing metrics.

Maya (eng-sre): seeing a spike in 504s from gateway frontends to backend inference nodes. error ratio ~12% over 2 mins.

Jorge (netops): any changes to peering/route tables in the last hour?

Samira (support): customer impact: two enterprise customers reported request failures and retries stuck, one experiencing consistent 504s in EU region.

Asha (oncall): no infra deploys reported by deploy-bot in last hour. deploy-bot: no deploys.

Maya (eng-sre): collecting conntrack and nat metrics from transit appliances now. preliminary: conntrack usage ~84%, ephemeral port exhaustion rising on gw-nat-02.

Jorge (netops): running tcpdump on gw-nat-02: I see asymmetric src/dst for some flows, SYN landed on nat-02 but return is routed via nat-01 -> return gets dropped by conntrack.

Maya (eng-sre): that would explain the 504s/timeouts. requests get to backend then responses never correlate back.

Asha (oncall): mitigation options?

Jorge (netops): immediate: pin affected subnet route to nat-02 (force symmetric path) or enable reverse path policy to steer return. medium: increase SNAT port pool / reserve additional ephemeral ranges.

Maya (eng-sre): can we fail traffic to fallback gateway in another AZ while we patch routing? Fallback has spare capacity.

Asha (oncall): Initiating mitigation: 1) Add route override for customer-subnet-7 -> nat-02 (temporary, 5min) 2) Scale NAT translation pool on nat-01/02: bump ephemeral ports by +50% 3) Enable aggressive conntrack timeout reset on stale entries.

Jorge (netops): applying route override now. patching route table rtb-priv-eu-west-3 -> target nat-02.

Maya (eng-sre): rolling out QoS change: lower keepalive on idle connections to free conntrack slots: echo 30 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_keepalive_time on transit nodes.

Samira (support): letting impacted customers know we’re mitigating, asking for any additional logs from them.

Elena (customer-obs): adding customer error-rate panels and open tickets to incident doc. tagging customers for postmortem follow-up.

(1 min later) Jorge (netops): route override in place. initial 1-min metrics: 504s dropping from 12% -> 5%.

Asha (oncall): good. continuing monitoring, will keep override for 15 mins while we validate.

Maya (eng-sre): conntrack freed up after keepalive change, ephemeral usage dropped ~30%. active translations stable.

Jorge (netops): applying ephemeral port bump now: expanded range on nat-01/02, verifying via /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range and nat appliance settings.

Maya (eng-sre): confirming backend app instances reporting normal responses again; tail of access logs show 200 after route change.

Samira (support): Customers A and B reporting improvement, retries succeeding.

Asha (oncall): lowering paging sensitivity to watch; keeping this thread open for 30m. tagging owners for follow-up: @Maya -> postmortem, @Jorge -> root cause & route automation, @Elena -> customer comms.

Jorge (netops): root cause hypothesis: route flap during maintenance window in peering edge caused a subset of flows to egress via a different NAT appliance, leading to conntrack mismatch (asymmetric NAT). fix: add route preference and automated affinity for long-lived flows + health-check based route selection.

Maya (eng-sre): action items before close: 1) revert route override after 15m if stable 2) run conntrack audit across nat fleet 3) add alert for asymmetric flow ratio >2% 4) add doc for emergency route pinning.

Asha (oncall): leaving handover to Maya for postmortem follow-up. I will remain oncall for 10 more mins then hand to next oncall if needed.

(20 mins later) Maya (eng-sre): metrics stable, 504 rate back to baseline ~0.5%. reverting route override now.

Jorge (netops): route override removed. monitoring.

Samira (support): customers confirmed stable, closing incident from support side. preparing summary message to customers.

Elena (customer-obs): logged incident in tracking board, assigned postmortem owners.

Maya (eng-sre): postmortem notes draft: cause = asymmetric egress after peering route flap -> partial return paths via different NAT appliance -> conntrack mismatches -> increased timeouts. Mitigations applied: route pinning, ephemeral port expansion, conntrack tuning, keepalive reduction. Long-term: route affinity automation, healthcheck-driven egress selection, increase conntrack headroom.

deploy-bot: reminder: no deploys performed during incident window.

Asha (oncall): closing thread: incident mitigated, customers notified, postmortem assigned.

Maya (eng-sre): will open RFC for automatic egress affinity in infra backlog.

-- end of thread --
